problem_statement: The paper frames the task as predicting global gold price movements for finance and investment, treating gold as a safe-haven asset whose daily price fluctuations matter to investors. It says the goal is to predict whether gold prices will rise or fall so that investors can make informed decisions.
problem_statement_quotes: The price of gold has garnered significant attention in the world of finance and investment due to its role as a safe haven asset and an indicator of global economic stability.
An inherent risk of investing in gold is the daily fluctuation in prices, which can rise, fall, or remain stable.
Investors are constantly seeking accurate ways to predict gold price movements in order to make informed investment decisions.
It is widely acknowledged that accurately and consistently predicting the gold price movements, exchange rate, and whether the gold price will rise or fall is very challenging.
classical_baseline: The paper compares against classical artificial neural network approaches, especially backpropagation, multilayer perceptron, and other conventional prediction methods such as Naive Bayes and RBFNN in related work. It treats these as the existing baseline family for gold-price prediction.
classical_baseline_quotes: While classic algorithms like artificial neural networks have been used for gold price prediction, they often struggle with analyzing complex data and identifying the hidden patterns within large datasets.
Research [28] and [29] suggest that backpropagation and multilayer perceptron models require a significant amount of computational time to achieve optimal results.
The main reference for this research is a study [32] entitled ” Prediksi Harga Emas dengan Menggunakan Metode Naïve Bayes dalam Investasi untuk Meminimalisasi Resiko”.
Research [30] focuses on "Prediksi Harga Emas Menggunakan Metode BiLSTM Neural Network." In this study, the method used for the prediction is Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN).
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical methods struggle with complex data, hidden patterns, and large datasets, and that accurate, consistent prediction is very challenging. It also says some classical models need many epochs or long execution times to reach good results, which makes them computationally costly.
classical_difficulty_quotes: While classic algorithms like artificial neural networks have been used for gold price prediction, they often struggle with analyzing complex data and identifying the hidden patterns within large datasets.
It is widely acknowledged that accurately and consistently predicting the gold price movements, exchange rate, and whether the gold price will rise or fall is very challenging.
As the number of input parameters and layers in neural networks increases, the computational costs increase significantly [19], [20].
Research [28] and [29] suggest that backpropagation and multilayer perceptron models require a significant amount of computational time to achieve optimal results.
In research [28], backpropagation took 3000 epochs to achieve optimal results.
business_stakes: The paper says the stakes are investment decision-making and risk reduction: accurate prediction is needed so investors can make profitable decisions and minimize risk. It also links gold to global economic stability, which raises the practical importance of the forecasting task.
business_stakes_quotes: The price of gold has garnered significant attention in the world of finance and investment due to its role as a safe haven asset and an indicator of global economic stability.
Investors are constantly seeking accurate ways to predict gold price movements in order to make informed investment decisions.
Market participants are always looking for ways to accurately predict the movements of gold price in order to make profitable investment decisions [5].
The main reference notes that the accuracy results for making predictions are still suboptimal. As a result, researchers have turned to the quantum perceptron algorithm for making predictions.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is mostly algorithmic but does state finance/investment framing and classical limitations.
